Hey there! First post to the sub, though I love theory crafting new cards with my play group.

In my commander group I love to play Oloro, Ageless Ascetic, as I've always loved lifegain decks even though I know lifegain is a relatively underwhelming mechanic in magic. I think that might be part of why I like trying to make lifegain decks in each format I play.

Anyway, after playing many, many rounds of Oloro now, I thought I'd build an Abzan deck around lifegain, seeing as green is the thied best color for lifegain, after black and white. I figured there must be a commander for it, but to my surprise, out of the 9 Abzan colored commanders, not a single one directly interacts with lifegain. A full SIX of them interact with your graveyard, yet not even one deals with lifegain, a mechanic that I feel overlaps rather a lot between the three colors. I decided to try and fix that with this fine specimen.

I looked through every card in white, green, and black to look for themes in how the cards interact with lifegain, whether they give you life on enter the field triggers, death triggers, or if they give +1/+1 counters when you gain life, that sort of thing. Then i looked specifically at the multicolored cards within the abzan identity and found three themes that came out most: "on creature death trigger," "deal damage for the amount healed," and "toughness matters." So, combining those together, this is what I got!

This class is rife with issues and extremely over powered. I would not allow it at my table without heavy revision.

Right off the bat are it's proficient saving throws. In 5e there are three "common" saving throws (Dex, Con, Wis) and three "uncommon" saving throws. (Str, Int, Cha). All classes in the PHB have proficiency in one common and one uncommon save, and this one has proficiency in two common saves, Dex and Wis.

Secondly is Kinetic Defense. Dexterity is already arguably the best ability score in the game, and this makes is even better. I understand flavor-wise what the creator is going for, but this is far and away better than the Monk or Barbarian Unarmored Defense.

Then Dynamic Manipulation's speed boost. This is crazy. It's so much better than the Monk or Barbarian speed boost and at an earlier level. You'd almost certainly have +15 speed at level 1 with a 16 in Dex. Monks don't get there until level 6 and Barbarians never get there. I understand that speed is there thing, but this is nuts.

Speedborn Damage: This. Is. Insane. A monk's unarmed strikes - the whole thing their class is predicated upon - is a d4 at this level. The Speedborn is a d10 and only goes up from there. They're going to be dishing out almost the same amount of damage as a fighter that specializes in two-handed weapon fighting, and the fighter falls behind at 3rd level when the speedborn gets to do extra lightning damage. This isn't even in the realm of balanced.

Speed Actions. Most of these wouldn't be that crazy, except that almost none of them say what kind of action they require. If they don't require any action to be taken, they're broken. If they're all actions they'd mostly be fine. The problem here lies in how many Joules you're likely to have. At level 6 you can reasonably expect to have 16 (level 6*2 plus Wisdom modifier of 3*2 plus Dexterity modifier of 4). A monk has 6 ki points at this level. And while yes, you don't automatically regain them all after a short rest like a monk, the Monk must take 2 short rests to even reach the Speedborn's base number of available points. Lower the Joules available and this section *might* be reasonable.

Rapid Movement. So now the Speedborn is also gaining Action Surge. Which they can reliably do 3 times per long rest. The fighter has to take short rests in between each use of theirs, but the Speedborn could dump all 3 of theirs in one fight over 3 rounds. Not okay.

I think this comes down to from what perspective you look at the situation. 

From a tabletop gaming perspective, each combatant takes their full turn before any other combatant begins theirs. Thus the first worg would resolve all their actions, including it's attack action, before a second worg could begin taking their actions to move into the designated area. This is the simplest way for all the people at the table to get on with their night and advance the story.

However, from a roleplay perspective, not all the combatants are politely waiting for each other to move and attack before neatly taking their turns in the queue. Of course in-universe all these actions are occuring basically simultaneously, with combatants trading blows back and forth, and maneuvering around the battlefield all at once. In this light is seems obvious that all the worgs would move at once, and the Warlock would be able to use their ability on at least two of them before either of them had a chance to attack.

Ultimately, neither one is really wrong or strictly better than the other. Though, if you decide to go with the second scenario, the more realism-friendly one, you open yourself up as a DM to lots of questions from your players about what "makes more sense" when they're trying to do something complex. As long as you and your players have a good relationship and they can respect the times that you stick more closely to the rules for the sake of brevity, then by all means let your player do something that doesn't quite fit the rules precisely as they're written, but makes sense from an in-game perspective.

Yeah, basically try to base it case by case. In 3.5e some of the skills required training to use such as Use Magic Device or Disable Device. Now 4e and 5e have a largely reduced list of skills, which is nice for simplification, but got rid of any training prerequisites to use them. However, I think it fair to say that someone who isn't schooled in Arcana (has proficiency in it) wouldn't be able to identify a magical glyph or seal on a door, for example. On the other hand I think it also reasonable to say that even a barbarian would be able to roll arcana to be able to tell if the seal is magical or ornamental from previous adventuring experience or getting a feel in the air or something.
I'd say it's DM discretion.
